title: Spray seascape

reference.source: Reference 21: airbrush seascape illustration, 894 × 1166 px PNG.
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: Flat inks edge to edge, every transition an airbrush spray of crisp 3 px dots whose landing chance falls off over about 80 px from a frisket edge, with black keying the silhouettes and the shadowed undersides.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 894 × 1166 and every length scales with the canvas

dot.does: Diameter of a spray dot. The reference's isolated green dots measure 3.2 px.

falloff.does: Distance over which a spray thins from solid to nothing past a frisket edge.

grain.does: Per-pixel grain of the flat inks and the light speckle in the blues, 1.7 % of pixels at 1.

ink.does: Width of the black keylines: hill tops, waterlines, pebble rims, posts and the robot.

shadow.does: Strength of the black spray on the shadowed undersides of land and pebbles.

light.does: Which side of each mass stays yellow and which side takes the black.

lit.does: Depth of yellow left bare under each hill top before the green spray starts.

horizon.does: Height of the sea line; the reference's keyline sits at 0.462.

cloud.does: How far the white sky wedge climbs above the horizon at its high end.

pink.does: Density of the pink spray along the edge of the white wedge.

speck.does: Sparse white spray dots in the blue above the cloud band.

waves.does: Rows of white foam dots across the sea, spaced wider toward the shore.

foam.does: Density of the white dots on the foam rows.

posts.does: Posts in the shallows, receding toward the horizon; green over black, foam at the foot.

hills.does: Rounded masses stacked back to front on the near shore.

beach.does: Depth of the white foam beach along the foot of the sheet.

pebbles.does: Black-rimmed pebbles in the beach foam, blue with a green patch.

robot.does: Height of the seated robot, 84 px at 1, 101 px at the default 1.2; 0 removes it.

robotX.does: Where across the sheet the robot sits; it lands on the first land below the horizon at that point and tilts with the slope.

scatter.does: Random shift in the land masses' positions.

seed.does: Re-rolls islands, rows, pebbles and every spray dot.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Cloud band: pink dots over blue, about half and half, thinning over 80 px into the white wedge below.

techniques.name: Tone
techniques.implementation: Hill top: bare yellow under the keyline, then green dots 3.2 px across thickening downhill.

techniques.name: Ink
techniques.implementation: Shadow edge: black spray at most 0.8 dense along the underside of a lobe, 77 % black here.

techniques.name: Paper
techniques.implementation: Flat sky: blue grain of 7.5 levels with about 6 % sparse white spray dots.

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Pebble beach: black-rimmed blue pebbles in white foam, green patches with black stipple under them.

pass_order: flats: sky blue over sea blue at the horizon (0.462 of the height), a white wedge rising under the cloud band
sky spray: blue falling into the white over the falloff, a pink band along the wedge edge, sparse white dots up in the blue
islands: yellow domes on the horizon, green sprayed up from the waterline, a black key; keys run at the black key slider (0.75) times 1.5 px for islands, 2 px for land, 2.2 px for the horizon
sea: rows of white foam dots (stretched 1.7:1) widening and spacing out toward the shore, a white shore band, posts in the shallows, green over black with foam at the foot

land: six rounded masses back to front. Each is a frisket: yellow inside, green sprayed up from below over the falloff and bent by a slow noise into lobes, black sprayed along the shadowed underside at most 0.8 dense, a key only where it stands against sea or sky
beach: black sprayed up at the land's foot, white foam with blue and green spray, 32 black-rimmed blue pebbles with a green patch and black stipple under it
robot: mgRobot seated on the near hill, tilted to the slope, drawn into the white, yellow and pink plates with a black key and a green cast shadow

print: every dot and key is a coverage-weighted disc (1 px edge); each ink then takes its measured grain: a skewed pixel noise with a 2 px share, a 30 to 90 px mottle on blue and green, sparse light specks that cluster

inks_browser_p50.method: median inside 5 × 5 eroded ink regions, reference decoded in the bench page; the file's raw values (blue [100, 146, 202], green [59, 126, 95]) differ through its ICC profile

ink_shares.method: nearest of six inks over every pixel

spray_dot_diameter_px.method: components after a 2 × 2 opening, area 3 px and up, diameter from area

dot_edge_px.method: cross-sections of isolated green dots on yellow: 225, 188, 79, 111, 86, 127, 234

sky_grain.method: flat sky 600 × 200 px; specks are pixels 15 above the median

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Shore blue palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: The shoreline is generated, so the cloud edge, hill spray, shadow edge and pebble beach rects were re-picked after the rebuild with search.py's window scan, each restricted to the matching zone of the render (sky band, land, beach). The flat sky and the whole plate compare in place. Inks are the reference's colors as the browser decodes them through its embedded ICC profile, which is how the bench reads it.

limits: Bench mean about 0.96, under 98 %. The lowest metrics are the cloud edge and shadow edge tone histograms (0.87): the reference's dots carry soft 1 to 2 px rims, so a quarter of its pixels sit 21 or more levels from any ink, and the render's 1 px dot edges leave fewer in-between values. A wider dot edge was tried (1.4 and 1.8 px) and scored the same or lower, and it softens the dots the brief asks to keep crisp.
The flat sky spectrum scores 0.93: the reference's mottle has a specific energy at 30 to 60 px that two value noises approximate but do not match.
The pebble beach black ink scores 0.91: the reference's black stipple there is mixed with green at the dot rims, so its mean black reads greener than the render's.
The shoreline is generated, so searched windows compare spray material at different places, not the same rocks.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
